results.title: US-Russia Tax Treaty Update FAQs
results.body:
• Does this change apply to authors in all regions of Russia?

    Yes, this change applies to all authors who are tax residents of Russia, regardless of the region in which they live.

  • If payouts are still restricted, how does this affect my total earnings or tax obligations?

    US withholding tax is applied at the point when income is earned (for example, when a sale is made), not when payouts are made. Although current sanctions mean that Envato is still unable to process payouts to Russian authors, tax obligations under US law still apply at the time of earning.

  • What happens to earnings made between 16 August 2024 and 1 August 2025 - what tax rate applies?

    We will apply the new 30% withholding tax rate to US-sourced earnings made from 1 August 2025 onwards. No changes will be made to earnings generated before that date, including those made between 16 August 2024 and 31 July 2025.

  • Do I need to submit a new W-8 form or take any action with the IRS or Envato?

    No action is required from you at this time. We will update the applicable withholding rate on our end based on your existing tax information.

  • What if I have more questions?

    For questions related to how this change might affect your personal tax situation, we recommend speaking with a tax advisor in your region. For any Envato account or platform-related questions, please contact Envato Support.

results.name: US Based authors - W9 Tax Requirements
results.title: US Based authors - W9 Tax Requirements
results.body:
Summary: This article details how to complete and submit your W-9 Form if you’re an Author in the US, as well as some FAQs. All authors must complete a tax form in order to receive payments.

Your situation will determine which tax form you need to fill out.

- US persons are required to fill out a W9 form (you are here!)
- Non-US individuals will need to fill out a W-8BENform,
- Non-US organizations will need to fill out a W-8BEN-E.form.

Important: While we cannot provide you with tax advice, we have put together this article to help you through the process. This has the caveat that you should always seek advice from a professional accountant/tax advisor because we are not authorised to advise about your specific tax situation, including filling out your specific tax form.

Please note that tax forms submitted between 1 July 2026 and September 2026, will not take effect until September 2026. This is due to upcoming changes in our tax application. Please see this article: Upcoming Tax Changes - July 2026 for more information.

What’s required?

All Authors on Envato must provide a valid tax form to ensure Royalty Withholding Taxes (RWT) are applied correctly to your earnings.

An Author account has one owner, whose details should be in the tax information. That owner can be a corporation or other type of entity. Note that if you are a partnership, partners must nominate one partner to submit their tax information and withdrawals will only be made to the nominated partner.

For US Based Authors;

  • US Authors (individual or corporations) are required to complete a standard IRS form called the Form W-9 which includes some basic information about you, including a Tax Identification Number (TIN). The TIN can either be your Social Security Number (SSN) or the Employer Identification Number (EIN) of your business.
  • If you do not provide your tax information, we cannot remit your payments. In addition, we may be required to apply backup withholding tax of 24% on all your earnings.
  • Any tax withheld by Envato will be remitted to the IRS, and not held by Envato. We will also be preparing and filing Forms 1099 with the IRS that will show the amount of your gross earnings and taxes we paid from your earnings.
  • You will be provided a copy of your Form 1099 no later than January 31 in the year following the year you made your earnings.
  • These forms can be provided to your tax accountant to assist with claiming any tax credits that may be available.

How to Submit your Tax form

The form is available under Tax Information on your Author Home page, or directly via the link:

https://author.envato.com/tax_information and selecting Complete a Tax Form.

Select whether you are a US person or not a US person

.A U.S person is:

  • An individual who is a US citizen or US resident alien.
  • A partnership, limited liability company, corporation, company, or association created or organized in the United States or under the laws of the United States.
  • An estate (other than a foreign estate), or
  • A domestic trust (as defined in US tax regulations).

If you are not a U.S Person, select “I am not a U.S Person” and you will continue to the W8 Form. You can find more information on that here: W-8 Requirements for non US Authors.

Part 1 - Your Details

The next section of the form asks you for your personal details.

  • Provide details including your name, country, and postal address. Please ensure that you provide a complete address.
    • If you have already filled out your general payout information, you can choose to copy over most of this information from your profile.

TaxPayer Identification Number

You will also need to select in the drop down the Federal Tax Classification that applies to you, and enter in the relevant Tax Identification Number.

The tax classification on the Form W-9 refers to the type of legal entity you choose to run your business. The most common forms of businesses are:

  • Sole proprietorships
  • Partnerships
  • Corporations
  • Limited Liability Companies (LLC)

A Taxpayer Identification Number is an identification number issued by the United States’ Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the Social Security Administration (SSA). A Social Security Number (SSN) is issued by the SSA whereas all other TINs are issued by the IRS.

Depending on your selection, you will be directed to enter your identification number; either SSN or EIN.

 

 

Exemptions (optional)

If relevant to you, enter in your Exempt Payee code. Exemption codes apply to only certain entities, not individuals. If not relevant to you, click continue to go to the next step.

Part II - Certification

In the next part of the form, you need to certify that the information you’ve provided is correct.

Please make sure you understand all the items under this section. It is important to note that providing false information is subject to penalties under perjury.

You will also need to acknowledge the certification and provide your name as an electronic signature.

 

If you have already submitted a tax form and this is a new one, you will see a prompt to confirm that you want to Submit and void your previous form.

If you have any questions about this process, don’t hesitate to contact us by submitting a Help ticket. Alternatively, if you need further details, please see the following IRS Help articles:

  • Clarification for Form W-9
  • Single Member Limited Liability Companies

FAQs

  • Why do I have to submit Tax a tax form?

    This process is to help US Authors to report their earnings properly and to make sure that the appropriate taxes are applied.

  • What happens if I don’t complete my tax info until after withholding starts?

    As any amounts withheld prior to receiving your tax information will be sent to the IRS, we are unable to give you a refund. However, we will send you an earnings summary (Form 1099) which will show the earnings that you had and the taxes that you paid before your submitted your tax information. You may provide this statement to your tax adviser/accountant to see if you are eligible to claim tax credits in your country.

  • How secure is my tax information??

    We use Trolley, a trusted payments platform, to collect and store your tax information. Trolley is SOC 2 Type II certified and protects your data with bank-level 256-bit encryption and tokenization of sensitive details like government IDs and social security numbers. You can read more in Trolley's security policy (https://trolley.com/security-policies/)

  • What documentation will I get about amounts withheld?

    You will be able to see tax withheld on each payment in your Recent Payments section in Author Home, and we will also send you a Form 1099 on 31 January following the year you had your earnings.

  • Should I be seeking tax or legal advice?

    Anytime you earn money as an independent contractor, freelancer, or through an online service, you should make sure you have informed your accountant or tax advisor so they can help make sure that you are correctly paying your taxes.

  • What if there are multiple owners of the account?

    Envato Market enters into a legal agreement with the person who creates an account and agrees to the terms and conditions. An Author account has one owner, and it is their details which should be in the tax formThat owner can be a corporation or other type of entity. Note that if you are a Partnership, Partners must nominate one partner to submit a W-8 or W-9. Withdrawals will only be made to the nominated account.

  • What additional documentation will you be collecting?

    We regularly receive information from different sources and in cases where this information contradicts information you provided us we may need to get in touch with you and get clarification.

  • I’m a US Person, but I reside elsewhere or am travelling

    You should consult your tax advisor. All authors must complete a Tax form, and it is up to you to ensure the information is correct and up to date.

  • Are prizes from Envato taxed?

    Any income received as "prizes and awards" will relate to non-royalty income.

results.name: Non-US Based authors - W8 Tax Requirements
results.title: Non-US Based authors - W8 Tax Requirements
results.body:
Summary: This article details how to complete and submit your W-8 Forms, for Authors and organizations outside of the US, as well as some FAQs.

Your situation will determine which tax form you need to fill out.

- US persons are required to fill out a W9 form
- Non-US individuals will need to fill out a W-8BEN form, and Non-US individuals organistions will need a W-8BEN-E form (you are here!)
 

Important: While we cannot provide you with tax advice, we have put together this article to help you through the process. This has the caveat that you should always seek advice from a professional accountant/tax advisor because we are not authorised to advise about your specific tax situation, including filling out your specific tax form.

Please note that tax forms submitted between 1 July 2026 and September 2026, will not take effect until September 2026. This is due to upcoming changes in our tax application. Please see this article: Upcoming Tax Changes - July 2026 for more information.

What’s Required: 

All Authors on Envato must provide a valid tax form to ensure Royalty Withholding Taxes (RWT) are applied correctly to your earnings. 

An Author account has one owner, and it is their details which should be in the tax information.  That owner can be a corporation or other type of entity. Note that if you are a partnership, partners must nominate one partner to submit their tax information and withdrawals will only be made to the nominated partner.

Non-US Based authors:

  • Non-US Authors are required to complete a standard IRS form called Form W-8BEN (for individuals) or Form W-8BEN-E (for companies) which includes some basic information about you, including your Foreign Tax Identification Number (TIN) and country of residence.
  • The purpose of the Form W-8BEN and Form W-8BEN-E is to establish your identity and status as a non-U.S. person.
  •  If you do not submit your tax information, we can not remit your payments. In addition, your Market and Elements earnings from US buyers may be taxed at the highest rate of 30%, and will not benefit from a reduced withholding tax rate under a double tax agreement (if applicable).

Royalty Withholding Tax (RWT) for non-US Authors

Generally, transactions in digital creative content give rise to royalty earnings. If you are a non-US Author, your sales to US buyers may be subject to royalty withholding tax, depending on your country’s income tax treaty with the US.

US tax law provides that the US government may collect taxes for US source royalty income. A royalty is considered to be US sourced when the sale is made to a person residing within the US.

Accordingly, if you are a non-U.S. person, your sales to US buyers may be subject to royalty withholding tax of up to 30%.

However, if you are a resident of a country that has an income tax treaty with the U.S., you may be eligible for a reduced withholding tax rate. The full text of these treaties can be found on the IRS website.

A list of the applicable treaty royalty withholding tax rates can be found here. The applicable rates applied are based on the copyright classification.

Any tax withheld by Envato will be remitted to the IRS. We will also be preparing and filing form 1042s for the year ended 31 December with the IRS that will show the amount of your gross earnings from US buyers and taxes we paid from these earnings. You will be provided a copy of your Form 1042 from 15th March in the year following the year you made your earnings. These forms can be provided to your tax accountant to assist with claiming any tax credits that may be available in your home country.

How to Submit Your Tax Form 

The form is available under Tax Information on your Author Home page, or directly via the link: 

https://author.envato.com/tax_information and selecting Complete a Tax Form.

Select whether you are a US person or not a US person:

.A U.S person is: 

  • An individual who is a US citizen or US resident alien.
  • A partnership, limited liability company, corporation, company, or association created or organized in the United States or under the laws of the United States.
  • An estate (other than a foreign estate), or
  • A domestic trust (as defined in US tax regulations).

If you are a U.S Person, you will continue to the W9 Form. You can find more information on that here: W-9 Requirements for US Authors. 

Select if you are an individual or a corporation; 

Step 1 - Certification of No U.S. Activities (1 of 4)

You will be asked to certify that you are not classified as a US person or liable for US Taxes; that you are not a US citizen, resident or subject to US taxation. If you cannot certify this, you will continue to the W9 Form, and can read more on that here: W-9 Requirements for US Authors. 

Step 2 - Part 1; Your Details

The next section of the form asks you for your details.

  • Individual: Provide details including your name, country, and postal address. Please ensure that you provide a complete address. 
    • If you have already filled out your general payout information, you can choose to copy over most of this information from your profile. 
  • Corporation: Provide the Name of your Organisation, country and type of entity e.g corporation, simple trust, estate, partnership. 
    • Note that Envato enters into a legal agreement with the person who creates an account and agrees to the terms and conditions. An Author account has one owner, and it is their details which should be in the tax form. That owner can be a corporation or other type of entity.
    • Note that if you are a Partnership, Partners must nominate one partner to submit the form Withdrawals will only be made to the nominated account.

Individual - W-BEN Form 

Corporation: 

A disregarded entity is a business that has a single owner and is not a corporation under the US Regulations section 301.7701-2(b).

Chapter 3 status refers to, chapter 3 of the US Internal Revenue Code (Withholding of Tax on Nonresident Aliens and Foreign Corporations). Please refer to the IRS instructions for further details https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/iw8bene.pdf . For your Chapter 3 status, please select the type that represents your classification (for example, corporation, trust, estate, etc). By selecting a particular type, you are representing that you qualify for the classification indicated.

NOTE: For a Partnership, you will see an additional question: Is the entity a hybrid making a treaty claim? A “Yes” answer indicates that you are an intermediary or flow-through entity; i.e. a foreign business receiving money from the U.S., but you are not the true beneficial owner of that money. A prompt to complete a W-8IMY form will follow. However Envato is not able to enter into agreements with these entities nor can we accept W-8IMY forms. You would need to supply us with a W8/W9 Form which would be from the beneficial owner of the income.

Part 2 - Tax Identification Number

Next, the form asks for your tax identification type and number. You may provide your Foreign Tax ID Number, which is the number that you use when you submit your tax return or pay taxes in your country.

If you’re unable to provide your tax identification number you won’t be able to claim a tax treaty benefit and your earnings from US customers will be subject to 30% withholding rate.

To find your Foreign Tax ID Number, please see the guidance provided by the various jurisdictions and the OECD here. Alternatively, you may also find the guidance provided by the European Commission.

Once you confirm your information, if you’re from a country that has a treaty with the US you’ll be shown the treaty article number and tax rate relevant to your country. You can find this information in this extract table from the IRS. You can also view the full table on the IRS website (Table 1). 

If your country is not on this table, that means your country does not have a treaty with the US. If you’re from a country that doesn’t have a treaty with the US, you will go straight to the next confirmation step. 

Step 3: Confirmation

Page 3 of 4 is a chance to review your details. Ensure all of your details are correct before moving on.

Step 4 - Certification

In the final section of the form, you’re required to certify the information you’ve provided is correct.

Please make sure you understand all the items under this section. The purpose of the Form W-8 is to establish your identity and status as a non-U.S. person, that you are the beneficial owner of the revenue and whether a lower rate of withholding applies as the result of a treaty claim. Even if your country does not have a treaty with the US, the form is used to establish that you are not a U.S. person. It is important to note that providing false information is subject to penalties under perjury.

You will also need to acknowledge the certification and provide your name as an electronic signature.


FAQs

  • What will we do with this information?

    When you complete your tax information, W-8BEN or W-8BENE, you are certifying that you are not a US person. The Form W-8BEN or Form W-8BEN-E form will determine the appropriate withholding tax rate that will be applied to your sales to US customers, if any. At the end of each calendar year we'll send to you and the IRS a summary of your earnings from US customers, Form 1042, so that you can accurately report your income to your local tax authorities and claim any credits for the taxes withheld and remitted to the IRS.

  • I don’t have a foreign tax identity number, what should I do?

    If your country of residence has a tax treaty with the US, you need to include your Foreign Tax ID Number on your tax information. Your Foreign Tax ID Number is usually the number that you quote when you lodge your tax return or pay tax in your own country. To find your Foreign Tax ID Number, please see the guidance provided by the various jurisdictions and the OECD here. Alternatively, you may also find the guidance provided by the European Commission.

  • I need a letter from Envato to support my W-7 application for a Tax Identity Number, who should I contact?

    As part of the IRS ITIN application process, an Author may be required to provide a signed letter or document from Envato, on official letterhead, showing their name and verifying that an ITIN is required to make distributions to them during the current tax year that are subject to IRS information reporting and/or federal tax withholding. If you require this document, please contact us. You will need to provide us with your full name that matches the W-7 application. The IRS will not accept Usernames.

  • What happens if I don’t provide a US TIN or a foreign tax identity number?

    If you are a non-US Person from a country with a tax treaty with the US, we can’t apply the benefit of the treaty rate reduction and will be required to apply royalty withholding tax at the full rate of 30%. If you’re in a country that has no tax treaty with the US, unfortunately, we won’t be able to reduce the royalty withholding tax rate of 30%.

  • Does this apply to US Authors?

    No, this article relates to a US tax form from the IRS (the US tax authority) for non-US Persons. However all authors must complete a tax form - A separate form (W-9) is applicable for US Authors.

  • What is this process for?

    This process is needed to meet the IRS’ requirement that the appropriate taxes are applied to sales of digital products considered to be royalties.

  • What happens if I don’t complete my tax info until after I am taxed at the highest rate of 30%?

    As any amounts withheld prior to receiving your tax information will be sent to the IRS, we are unable to give you a refund However, we will send you an earnings summary (Form 1042-S) which will show the earnings that you had and the taxes that you paid before your submitted your tax information. You may provide this statement to your tax adviser / accountant to see if you are eligible to claim tax credits in your country.

  • What happens if I pay Royalty Withholding Tax, but I also pay my tax in my home country?

    You should consult your accountant or tax advisor on how to ensure you’ve paid your correct taxes on your end of year tax return or if you are eligible to claim tax credits for the royalty withholding tax that was paid to the IRS.

  • How secure is my tax information stored with Envato?

    We take your privacy and information security seriously and will use industry standard practices to securely store any details you provide in this form.

  • What documentation will I get about amounts withheld?

    You will be able to see tax withheld on each payment in your Recent Payments section on your Author Dashboard and we will also send you a Form 1042 from 15 March following the year you had your earnings.

  • Should I be seeking tax or legal advice?

    Any time you earn money as an independent contractor, freelancer, or through an online service, you should make sure you have informed your accountant or tax advisor so they can help make sure that you are correctly paying your taxes.

  • What if there are multiple owners of the account?

    Envato Market enters into a legal agreement with the person who creates an account and agrees to the terms and conditions. If you are a US Person (a definition which includes Partnerships, LLCs amongst other things, as well as individuals) then you should complete the Form W-9 details. An Author account has one owner, and it is their details which should be in the tax form W-8. That owner can be a corporation or other type of entity. Note that if you are a Partnership, Partners must nominate one partner to submit the tax form. Withdrawals will only be made to the nominated account.

  • If I already pay taxes in my country for my earnings on Envato do I still need to provide the tax information Envato is asking for?

    If you do not provide your tax information, Envato cannot pay you and may also be required to withhold 30% from your gross earnings from US buyers.

  • Will I be taxed twice if my country does not have a tax treaty with the US?

    The answer will depend entirely on your country of residence.

  • If my country has a tax treaty with the US how much tax will be withheld from my earnings?

    Generally, an income tax treaty will provide for a reduced or zero rate of withholding on royalty income.

  • If I am a citizen of another country but live and maintain a residence or address in the US does that affect the tax information I must supply to Envato?

    You will need to speak with your tax advisor, as circumstances and opinions may differ. We recommend that you speak with your tax advisor, as this may be a very fact specific question.

  • I am an international Author so why is the U.S. taxing me?

    US tax law provides that the US government may collect taxes for US source royalty income. A royalty is considered to be US sourced when the sale is made to a person residing within the US.

  • How will my earnings as an Author be calculated after withholding tax is applied?

    Envato will apply royalty withholding taxes at the time of payment instead of at the time of earning.
    Envato Market: this applies to earnings from August 1st 2026. September will be the first payment that this applies to (August earnings, paid in September).
    Envato Elements: this applies to earnings from July 1st 2026. September will be the first Elements payment that this applies to (July earnings, paid in September).
    For Envato Market sales, RWT only applies to sales to U.S based buyers; known as US sourced income.
    Example for Envato Market; Let's use an example where you make a sale of a WordPress theme for $49 to a U.S. buyer: The first thing is that in a $49 WordPress theme sale, $12 of that is our Envato Fixed Buyer Fee directly to the buyer. So your Item Price is $37.
    Step 1: $49 - $12 = $37 is the Author's Item Price
    Step 2: The Author fee is detracted, which is usually 50%.
    50% of $37 = $18.50
    Step 3 - RWT Applied
    Lastly, when all your earnings are collated in your balance, we will attempt to pay them out to you when they reach over our minimum payout threshold of $50. We apply US Royalty Withholding Tax (RWT) and send this to the IRS at the time we pay you. This changes based on the treaty rate between your country and the USA. Again, using the above example, let's say the Author's country does have a treaty with the US and the RWT rate is 10%. 10% would be withdrawn from the Item Price (10% of $37 is $3.70) which will be remitted to the IRS. The final amount you would get paid is: $37 - $18.50 - $3.70 = $14.80
    Example for Envato Elements:
    Your Envato Elements earnings are collated and added to your Balance, and we will attempt to pay them out to you when you reach over the minimum payout threshold of $50.
    Tax is applied at the time of payment; so let’s say you have a $100 payment. We will determine how much of your $100 earnings related to US-Sourced income. I.e. what portion of your earnings related to a US subscriber. If $30 of your earnings was used by US subscribers, this would be the amount we calculate RWT. If your country has a tax treaty with the US resulting in a RWT rate of 10%, we will apply 10% RWT to the $30. Therefore, $3 would be withdrawn from this payment and remitted to the IRS resulting in your payout to be $97.

results.name: Author's Guide to Envato Statements & Documents
results.title: Author's Guide to Envato Statements & Documents
results.body:
Summary: This guide is designed to assist with questions regarding your statement and Envato documents.

Your Statement

Your statement will provide you with your total sales (the value of all sales you’ve made to buyers), your total expenses to Envato (the value of all author and SWIFT fees), and details of any other transactions your account may have registered such as referral earnings and purchases. 

 

This article will help you to Download Statement Data as CSV.

 

Sales will appear on your statement as separate line items. Bundled Item Support and any purchased support extensions will appear as separate line items (if applicable).

Unsupported Items

Items that do not come with support will appear on your statement in two lines:

  • Item price
  • Author fee

Supported Items

Items that come bundled with 6 months of support will appear as four lines:

  • Item price
  • Author fee for the item
  • Price of included support component
  • Author fee for included support component

 

If the customer purchases a support upgrade (or extension), you will see an additional two line items on your statement:

  • Price of extended support
  • Author fee for extended support

 

The author fee statement lines show the amount you have paid Envato as an author fee. There are separate lines for author fees relating to sales (Author Fee for sale) and item support (Author Fee for included/extended support).

 

Your Invoices

You can access the invoice that was issued to the buyer for the purchase of an item by clicking the invoice number on your Statement.

Your invoices will look like this:

 

 

Monthly Service Fee Invoice

Authors receive a monthly service fee invoice from Envato for all author fees (item sale and item support), and SWIFT fees that were charged during the month. 

Service fee invoices are issued on the 1st of the month:

Eg. The service fee invoice for the month of February 2025 issued on March 1, 2025

 

You can access your Monthly Service Fee Invoice at any time. To do this:

  1. Go to your Statement Page (https://themeforest.net/user/USERNAME/statement)
  2. Click the Monthly Service Fees drop down and select the month you wish to view.
  3. Click Download on the right. The monthly service fee invoice will open in a new tab.

 

 

NOTE: SWIFT fees will appear on the invoice for the month the payout is processed (paid).

The Total (at the bottom of your Monthly Service Fee Invoice), is the sum of all author, SWIFT fees. Please note that:

  • If no sales and no SWIFT payout occurs during any given month, no service fee invoice will be generated.
  • If no sales are made during the month,  but a payout is still processed via SWIFT, your service fee invoice will detail a SWIFT fee only.

     

Envato will provide a service fee invoice showing any taxes that are charged during a month. That means if you changed your address mid-month you may see multiple invoices.  This example shows an author selling from Australia (attracting GST), Quebec(QST) and from a country where tax does not apply to author fees, all in January 2019.

Invoice details

To ensure all your documents are correctly addressed, please enter or update your billing address details. For more information please refer to How Do I Add Or Change My Billing Address?

All financial activity on an account is in the name of the account owner (the person who signed up to the account and agreed to the terms and conditions). We act under the account owner’s direction to payout earnings to the payout account you select.

This article will guide you on how to Add a Company Number or Custom Invoice Footer.

 

Company and buyer details

Please note that only you can see your full billing details; the buyer will see only your company name (or full name and username if you do not have company name), your city, state/province and country. Conversely, you can see the buyer’s company name (or first initial and last name if they do not have a company name), city, state/province, and country.

 

Tax & Value Added Tax (EU VAT)

Aside from specific taxes that are managed by Envato (these are referenced in the Terms and Conditions), it is your responsibility to manage and comply with taxes and laws in your country.

To help you manage your tax compliance, we’ve put together some information. You’ll need to select which guide is relevant to you from the list below:

  • Tax Information and Form W-8 Requirements for non-US Authors
  • Tax Information and Form W-9 Requirements for US Authors

For general VAT information please see our EU VAT overview or EU VAT information for authors article.

AU GST

For general information please go to the GST summary article or more specifically AU GST Information for authors article.

US Sales Tax

To read more about US sales tax how we can help our US authors meet their tax obligations please visit this article.

 If you have questions about taxes please contact taxinfo@envato.com

 

What is a Credit Note?

A credit note is when a reversal of an invoice occurs (negative invoice). When an invoice has been generated and the transaction is cancelled or voided a credit note is issued to support it.

results.title: Withholding Taxes with Envato Elements and Envato Market
results.body:
Summary: Envato applies US Royalty Withholding Tax (US RWT) to US-sourced earnings on Envato Market and Envato Elements (effective 1 January 2026). AU Royalty Withholding Tax (AU RWT) will no longer be withheld on either platform, making your 2026 AU RWT summary the final one you will receive.

Envato Market

When you sell items on Envato Market, you sell directly to the customer. When a US-based buyer purchases your item, US Royalty Withholding Tax (US RWT) applies.

From 1 January 2026, Envato will no longer withhold AU Royalty Withholding Tax (AU RWT) on your Market earnings. The 2026 AU RWT summary (covering the period to 31 December 2025) is the final AU tax summary you will receive for Envato Market. You will continue to receive your 1042-S or 1099-MISC tax summary for your US-sourced earnings as normal. For more details on these forms, please visit our Tax Forms 1099 and 1042 FAQs.

Withheld tax appears on your tax summaries. Most authors can claim this amount as a tax credit in their home country.

Envato Elements

From 1 January 2026, US Royalty Withholding Tax (US RWT) applies when a US-based subscriber downloads your items on Envato Elements. Envato will no longer withhold AU RWT on your Elements earnings.

The 2026 AU RWT summary (covering the period 1 July to 31 December 2025) is the final AU tax summary you will receive for your Elements earnings. Going forward, Envato will include your US-sourced Elements earnings in your 1042-S or 1099-MISC tax summary. For more details on these forms, please visit our Tax Forms 1099 and 1042 FAQs.

Envato classifies a subscriber as US-based if the billing address country on their invoice is the United States (country code: US). This tax applies to non-US authors only.

The default US RWT rate is 30%. If your country shares a tax treaty with the United States and you submit a valid W-form, Envato applies your lower applicable treaty rate. If you do not submit a W-form, the default rate of 30% may apply regardless of your country of residence.

Depending on the tax laws in your home country, you may be able to claim credits for taxes withheld in the US.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Do I need to complete a new tax form?

    All authors selling items on Envato must submit a valid tax form to ensure the correct Royalty Withholding Tax rates apply to their earnings. We can't send you any payments without a valid tax form. You can check your tax form status, and submit a new one, in your Author Dashboard.  You can also check the full US tax treaty list here.

results.title: Graphic File Packs and Bundles
results.body:
Summary: Summary: This article explains how you can upload multiple items to sell together as a Graphic Bundle, or upload similar sets of assets to be sold as a Pack. 

Table of Contents

  • What is a Bundle?
  • Bundle Requirements
  • What is a Pack?
  • Pack Requirements

What is a Bundle?

Bundles are item listings made from previously published files.

For example, a bundle of party flyers or a bundle of text effects.

Following image is an example of a collection, the files have a common theme, they are from the same category and exist as individual items on the Marketplace.

Bundle Requirements

  • Bundles must contain a minimum of 2 items and a maximum of 10 items.
  • All files in a bundle must be available as single items on the marketplace before a bundle is submitted.
  • Once an item is available for purchase as part of a collection, it should not be added to any subsequent bundles.
  • Bundle item descriptions must always reference and link to each individual item already available on the marketplace.
  • We recommended that individual item descriptions are updated to provide a link to the corresponding bundle once it is published

What is a Pack?

Packs have a common theme and style and require more than one item to be considered complete, for example, icons, lightroom filters and stationery. Packs are different to bundles, as packs do not need to be made up of items that are already approved as individual items.

Following image is an example of a file pack. The icons all have the same visual style with a common theme.

Pack Requirements

Before you upload a pack, ensure your items meets the following requirements:

  • Items in Packs must be relevant to each other (for example, things that are used together like Photoshop brushes)
  • Items must be from the same category.
  • Illustrations and designs must have the same style.
  • Color variations or minor detail shifts, will not be counted as unique enough variations to form a pack and will not be accepted.

The following table lists the minimum and maximum allowed file pack per category:

Exceptions to the maximum numbers above rule can be made based on group relevancy. For example, a pack of 50 U.S. state flags would be accepted because a complete set of US flags requires 50 items.

Example 1: An example of a minor variation, each vector is the same illustration with a different colour. This file would not be accepted. 

Example 2: An example of a vector pack, each vector is a different design with the same style.

Example 3: An example of a size exception, the item needs more than the  maximum allowed elements for the category to work as a complete set.

results.name: EU VAT FAQs
results.title: EU VAT FAQs
results.body:
• Does Envato have an EU VAT number?

    Yes, Envato’s VAT number is EU372009975.
    Ireland is our Member State of Identification for the VAT mini one stop-shop (MOSS) scheme.

    Prior to 1 October 2019 Envato’s VAT number was EU826409867
    UK was our Member State of Identification for the VAT mini one stop-shop (MOSS) scheme.

  • Envato is an Australian company, why do you need to do this?

    While Envato is an Australian company, Envato Market is a global marketplace with Authors and buyers around the world. Laws for online businesses such as ours are constantly evolving and there are ways in which other countries and laws impact on us and our responsibilities.

    Changes to the EU VAT telecommunications, broadcasting and electronic service rules mean that, from 2015, Envato will act as the supplier of digital items for the purpose of EU VAT collection.

  • Does this apply to non-EU Customers?

    No, this tax only applies to EU customers who do not have a valid EU VAT number. EU customers who have a valid EU VAT number must account for VAT using the Reverse Charge Mechanism.

  • Is my VAT information secure?

    We take your privacy and information security very seriously. Your information is stored securely using industry standards and practices.

  • My native country is within the EU, I’m currently living outside the EU or travelling. Which country do I select?

    Please ensure that the country you have selected is your country of residence for tax and legal purposes.

  • How do I update my country of residence?

    1. Select Settings from the menu under your username. You may then choose your country of residence from the Country drop-down.
    2. If you are an Author and have submitted your W Form, please update your country of residence by updating your tax information.

    Alternatively, you may click confirm on the banner heading, and select your country of residence from the dialog box that will appear.

  • How do I add my VAT number?

    1. Select Settings from the menu under your username or click confirm from the banner heading.
    2. If you choose an EU country, a new field will appear where you can enter your VAT number

results.name: Android App Requirements
results.title: Android App Requirements
results.body:
Summary: This article outlines Android App requirements. 

References:

  • https://developer.android.com/jetpack
  • https://developer.android.com/kotlin

Note: It is strongly recommended that your Android apps follow the Java and Kotlin Coding standards.

  • Apps must not have any redundant variables or methods (except if such variables and methods are meant to help adding further features).
  • Apps must close all streams used in  a finally clause when using the try-catch blocks.
  • Apps must not have hardcoded credentials for passwords or usernames.
  • If the app handles payment methods, it must have reliable 3rd party libraries.
  • Conditionals must evaluate different elements and must not always return true or false.

For example:

if (true)

while(true)

if( x>0 && x>0)

  • The code must cast the variables correctly to perform any arithmetic operation.
  • All strings used must be in the strings.xml file.
  • Variables must be local whenever possible, avoid using globals.
  • The app must have at least android API level 29 according to the new Playstore requirements.

Note: It is a good practice to use a code quality testing tool like sonarqube.

https://www.sonarqube.org/sonarqube-8-1/?gclid=EAIaIQobChMI3ZO-69Pv5wIVRr7ACh3-zAQsEAAYAiAAEgLzofD_BwE

results.name: Tax FAQs
results.title: Tax FAQs
results.body:
• Why has tax been withheld from my earnings?

    Envato is required by law to withhold certain taxes from your earnings as an author. The relevant section of the author agreement says:

    26. Withholding taxes: We may deduct or withhold from any amount payable to you under these Author Terms, including your earnings, an amount sufficient to satisfy any taxes (including withholding taxes) which we are required to withhold under applicable law. The rate of withholding taxes will depend on the jurisdiction where you are located and whether or not an applicable tax treaty exists. You are required to pay the full amount of any amount payable by you under these Author Terms and may not deduct any applicable taxes (including withholding taxes) from that amount, unless otherwise specified in an agreement with us or an invoice we issue.

    Envato is part of the Shutterstock group of companies, headquartered in the United States. The rights to pay you for your content sit with our US entity, which means US Royalty Withholding Tax (US RWT) applies to earnings sourced from US-based buyers on Envato Market, and US-based subscribers on Envato Elements. AU Royalty Withholding Tax (AU RWT) is no longer withheld on your Elements or Market earnings.

    The rate of US RWT that applies to you will depend on your country of residence and whether a tax treaty exists between your country and the United States. The default rate is 30%, but if your country has a US tax treaty and you have submitted a valid W-form, your applicable treaty rate will apply instead. We use the country information from your tax form (W8/W9) to calculate the amount to withhold. So please make sure you keep this information up to date if you move countries.

    If taxes are withheld from your earnings, we will provide you with a relevant document each year to help you manage your tax affairs — for example, a 1042-S or 1099-MISC tax summary — which you may be able to use to claim a credit on your tax return for the amount withheld.

  • Why would a customer ask for my tax information?

    From time to time you may receive requests from customers requesting a certificate of residency from you.

    There are a number of reasons why they might be doing this, a couple are:

    • Some countries, such as Poland, require customers to submit certain tax information that includes information about where they have purchased from, and how much they paid.
    • Some companies, such as US companies, may have a code of business conduct that requires proper certification from you as to your tax residency status.

    Please note that if you do not provide your tax information to the customer, they may not be able to purchase your item.

  • Do I need to pay taxes on my Envato Market earnings?

    Any earnings that you receive from Envato Market are your responsibility to manage appropriately within your local country. We cannot provide advice on how you should proceed to pay taxes on your author earnings as tax laws vary greatly from country to country.

    We encourage you to seek out professional advice on tax-law and filing taxes. While the specifics of your country’s tax laws might be different, there’s a good chance that your government still wants you to declare your income.

  • What happens to funds that are held by Envato?

    It is Envato’s policy to suspend access to and prohibit the removal of funds from author accounts that Envato determines are related to individuals located in or associated with restricted countries. Funds held in suspended accounts will be held by Envato until the user is permitted to receive them. If you believe your account has been suspended in error, please contact us immediately.
